evidence_items.explanation: The announcement introduces Photos as a standalone product within the preceding decade. Together with e2, it supplies a counterexample under the ordinary adoption-based reading.

evidence_items.locator: Numbered item 1; opening paragraph identifies monthly active users

receipt.public_excerpt: One hundred million of you are using Google Photos.

evidence_items.explanation: Google reported more than 100 million monthly active users five months after launch. That is substantial adoption, although it does not establish profitability.

evidence_items.publisher: The Daily Beast, republished by Yahoo Finance
evidence_items.locator: Paragraph beginning 'Google said it paid Character'
evidence_items.explanation: The reported payment matches the claim's amount. The article also attributes the desire to regain Shazeer to sources cited by the Wall Street Journal; it describes licensing rather than purchase of the entire startup.

metric_scope.metric: Payment to Character.AI for the licensing and hiring transaction

evidence_items.locator: Section 'Shazeer and Google', paragraph preceding the account of his departure
evidence_items.explanation: The surrounding account connects Google's refusal to release Meena with Shazeer and De Freitas leaving in 2021. This supports the reported departure story, but is secondary reporting rather than a firsthand explanation.

unresolved_gaps: No comparable pre-deal revenue or profit record establishes what 'barely made any money' means.
No supplied measure establishes that this was Google's most meaningful acquisition.
The evidence does not establish hiring Shazeer as the exclusive transaction purpose.
The generalization to every other hyperscaler was not independently established.
